placements.$craneBMCTNote: crane:BMCT:0 stood alone in the water. Its earlier correction projected it onto a straight line fitted from BMCT's other seven anchors, but at along-quay +301 m it lay ~300 m PAST the end of that line's data, so the fit was extrapolated off the curving wharf. It is now placed 70 m beyond crane:BMCT:2 - the last real crane in the row - so it sits on the quay among actual cranes instead of alone offshore. Positions before: [72.938557,18.945129] originally, then [72.940649,18.943373]. crane:BMCT:1 keeps its earlier correction (it lay INSIDE the fitted span, so no extrapolation was involved).
placements.$rakeNote: rake:T1 runs the rail corridor marked in red on the JNPA reference: a straight 1509 m line from above the BMCT gates, ESE along the port's landward boundary, ending at the JNPCT-G2 OUT gate. Georeferenced from the three gates labelled in that image — the line starts 140 m landward of BMCT-G2 (perpendicular to the BMCT-G2 -> JNPCT-G2 bearing of 134.55 deg) and ends on JNPCT-G2, giving a 139.87 deg run rounded to 140. 140 m of offset is what clears the BMCT gate structures: at 100 m the line passed 24 m from BMCT-G1, inside its 18 m canopy half-span. The anchor sits 200 m along the line because the rake trails 144 m of wagons behind it. The static track drawn by railTrackLayer() derives from this same anchor and heading, so the rails and the train can never drift apart. Previous: [72.949928,18.929288] heading 276 (JNPCT-G2 into the terminal).
placements.$rakeT2Note: rake:T2 restores the ORIGINAL central-yard siding line, at exactly the anchor and bearing rake:T1 held before the reference corridor was traced. The two lines are independent: T1 follows the red-line corridor, T2 keeps the original alignment, and each has its own rails drawn by railTrackLayer() and its own rake running on them.
placements.$yardNote: Yard blocks compacted 0.48x about each terminal's grid centroid (pitch 50/44 m -> 24/21 m); four NSIGT blocks nudged 1-6 m clear of the NSIGT truck route. JNPCT additionally tightened to the same 24/21 m pitch and moved 165 m LANDWARD: its yard sat 204-272 m behind the quay, ~150 m closer than every other terminal (351-472 m), leaving the terminal's open apron covered in isolated stacks. It now sits at 369-411 m, in line with the rest and still 1.5 km clear of its gates.
placements.$gateNote: North Gate and Central Gate are placed on the two real toll plazas OSM records INSIDE the Jawaharlal Nehru Port polygon (way 49499133), verified by Overpass is_in containment: 6 barrier=toll_booth nodes centred 18.952913,72.960401 sitting 45 m from the named "JNPT Terminal 1" access road (way 587671181), and 2 booths centred 18.935804,72.950528 on the "JNPT Terminal 2" branch (ways 807490638/807538918). Headings follow those road bearings (100 and 148 deg). The five terminal Entry Gates are NOT moved: OSM carries no terminal-gate feature, and this model's terminals sit 1.2-2.3 km west of the real JNPT road spine, so putting them on the real roads would detach them from the terminals they serve.
placements.$gateHeadingNote: Each gate canopy is squared across the road it stands on: heading = the bearing of that traced road at the gate. The toll-naka model spans 36 m across the carriageway and 14 m along it, and with no heading set every gate fell back to the port-wide 298 deg default. NSICT-G1 and NSIGT-G1 were the worst - 91-93 deg out, so their canopies blocked the road sideways instead of spanning it.
placements.$tugNote: tug moved 230 m further SEAWARD along the NSICT quay normal, from 421 m to ~651 m off the quay line. It was reported as looking beached on a mudflat edge. Its committed coordinate had not changed and no code touches it, so this is a judgement move, not a regression fix: the only trustworthy water references in the project are the hand-placed berthed vessels (141-493 m seaward), so pushing the tug beyond the furthest of them along the same axis is the one direction guaranteed to lead further from shore. Previous: [72.94631,18.963279].
